brief: RUNG 5, the observer: at 390 px wide the whole 138-cell town is a strip a thumb wide and a person is two pixels — every system built since #26 is invisible on a phone. Give the observer a way to look at ONE quarter. A control on the sill (a `#where` button next to #daytime/#season, or a double-tap on the canvas — the worker picks after reading how #daytime and OFFERS work) that eases the camera onto one of four frames — courtyard, street & allotments, plaza & river, far bank — and back to the wide view, on a real-clock ease like beginLapse's (never sim dt). The camera is originX/cellW/cellH inside resize()/project(): move the projection, not the world, and all hit-testing (nameAt, answersTouch, follow) keeps working because it already goes through project(). The cached layers (drawBlocks/drawGround) are rebuilt on resize today — measure with probes/ground-rebuilds.mjs and frame-cost.mjs what a zoom costs and whether the cache must be re-rendered or can be scaled. Join OFFERS (narrow-screen wording first: this offer matters most under 640 px). Prove it at 390 px with a shot of the plaza quarter where a person is readable.
successLooksLike: On a 390 px phone a visitor taps once and the plaza fills the frame — fountain, benches, people at readable size — and taps again to return to the wide view; on a 1400 px desktop the same control works and the wide view is still the default. Nothing that names or follows breaks under zoom.
avoid: No second canvas, no CSS transform on the canvas (the sill and hit-testing read canvas coordinates). Do not let a zoom persist across a page reload. Do not re-render the ground cache per frame while easing — either rebuild once at arrival or scale the bitmap during the ease.
